### Dataset used in this project

**The bundled data is synthetic.** It was generated by `generate_data.py` (seed 42) so that the project runs
offline and can be tested end to end. Brands (Vanta, Orbix, Kestrel, Lumio, Nexora, Zephyr, Aurum, Tessel) and all
models are fictional. Do not treat any price, spec or review as information about a real product.

| File | Rows | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `data/phones.csv` | 2,500 | One row per phone: brand, model, launch year, price in INR, RAM, storage, battery, charging watts, rear and selfie camera MP, camera quality score, screen size, refresh rate, processor benchmark score, 5G flag, store rating and rating count |
| `data/reviews.csv` | about 32,700 | One row per review: `phone_id`, `stars` (1 to 5) and review `text` |
| `data/dataset_info.json` | 1 | Metadata. The app shows a "demo data" notice while `type` is `synthetic` |

**How it was simulated.** Each phone is assigned a price tier. Spec groups (camera, battery, display, memory) can sit one
tier above or below the processor tier, so specs are only partly correlated. Price comes from a spec-based formula, a brand
premium and random noise. Reviews are built from sentence templates whose sentiment depends on how strong the phone is on each
aspect, with 8% of star ratings flipped to mimic real-world inconsistency.

**Consequences to state in your report.**
- Model scores (for example R² of the price model and accuracy of the sentiment model) describe how well the methods recover
  patterns that were simulated. They are not evidence about real phones.
- The price formula is dominated by the processor, so the processor dominates importance and ablation results.
- Review language is far more regular than real reviews, so real-data sentiment accuracy will usually be lower.

**Using real data.** Run `python prepare_real_data.py your_file.csv` after editing the column map at the top of that script.
Suggested public sources to search on Kaggle (check each dataset's licence and columns before use): *GSMArena Phone Dataset*
(by arwinneil), *Phones 2024* (by jakubkhalponiak), and Indian-market datasets titled "smartphones specifications prices India".
For reviews, search for "Amazon or Flipkart mobile phone reviews". Then re-run `python run_experiments.py`.
